question: How many viewers (millions, combined average across channels) will Spain's 26 November 2026 televised leaders' debate draw?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Spanish general-election leader debates 2015-2023, combined Kantar audience. It falls from about 9-10M (2015-19) to 5.9M (2023 cara a cara, Antena 3 + laSexta, July) and 4.1M (2023 RTVE three-way without Feijóo). Linear TV is weaker in 2026: the top programme on 12 Nov drew 4.1M, and a spokespeople debate on 14 Nov drew 1.3M. Factors pushing the number up: the Academia institutional signal can be picked up by several broadcasters (the 19 Nov cara a cara is on RTVE + Atresmedia and probably Mediaset), it is the first four-way with Sánchez and Feijóo together, November viewing is higher than July, and the campaign is tense. Factors pushing it down: viewer fatigue after the 19 Nov cara a cara and the 23 Nov debates, and carriage that is still unconfirmed (some sources list RTVE only; laSexta has Mesa Abierta scheduled that night). Market check: none found (Polymarket and Kalshi are blocked in Spain; nothing on Manifold). Median about 5.5M.
calls.dossier:
- Infobae 14 Nov 2026: the Academia de Televisión four-way (Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal, Colau) is set for Thu 26 Nov. It uses an institutional signal any broadcaster may carry, with the same 5 blocks as the 19 Nov cara a cara. Podemos/Montero's inclusion is pending at the JEC, which had earlier excluded Podemos from the laSexta debate.
- Doblelectura guide (Nov 2026): lists the 26 Nov debate as organiser Academia+RTVE, channels 'RTVE (unconfirmed)', time not announced. Vozpópuli calendar: 26 Nov broadcast on RTVE. laSexta 'Mesa Abierta' spokesperson panels are listed for 24 and 26 Nov.
- ABC 16 Nov 2026: the 19 Nov cara a cara airs at 22:00 on La 1, Canal 24h, Antena 3 and laSexta. Mediaset's channel is unspecified, but it moved GH VIP to accommodate the debate. Carriage for 26 Nov has not been reported.
- Other debates that week: the 23 Nov RTVE 8-spokesperson debate (22:00), and an Atresmedia four-way on 23 Nov whose status and line-up are uncertain.
- laSexta 14 Nov 2026 spokespeople debate: 11.9% share, about 1.3M average.
- Barlovento 12 Nov 2026: top programme was football on La 1 at 4.14M (30.9%); main news bulletins draw 2.1-2.3M.
- Historical combined audiences: 2015 four-way 9.23M; 2015 cara a cara 9.73M; 2016 four-way 10.5M; Apr 2019 RTVE four-way 8.89M and Atresmedia 9.48M; Nov 2019 five-way 8.63M on 12 channels; Jul 2023 cara a cara 5.91M (A3+laSexta only); Jul 2023 RTVE three-way without Feijóo 4.1M (La 1 3.46M + 24h 0.70M; eldiario/vertele).
- Base rates: over all debates 2015-2023 the median is about 9M, but over the post-2023 linear-TV regime only n=2 (5.9M on 2 channels; 4.1M on 2 RTVE channels with a main candidate absent).
- Resolves off Barlovento's combined debate-only figure for 26 Nov, not peak-minute or unique viewers. Value is in millions.
- Event window: the debate broadcast starting 26 Nov 2026 local time; as of 16 Nov, 0% elapsed (it is 10 days ahead).
- Searched without finding: confirmed 26 Nov channel carriage or start time; any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold; Polymarket and Kalshi are blocked in Spain since May 2026).

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Spanish general-election leader debates. The 2023 ones drew 4.0M (RTVE three-way) and 5.9M (cara a cara, only Antena 3 + laSexta, July). The 2015-2019 ones drew 8.6-10.5M when linear TV viewing was far higher. The 26 Nov four-way (Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal, Colau) is confirmed by press reports, with the Academia signal likely carried by RTVE and probably Atresmedia. Upward factors: final debate, November rather than July viewing, all four leaders, more channels. Downward factors: linear decline (170 min/day, a top football match drew only 4.1M on 12 Nov), fatigue after the 19 Nov cara a cara and the 23 Nov Atresmedia four-way, and the 14 Nov spokesperson debate drawing only ~1.3M. No human prediction or betting market was found. Median ~5.6M.

calls.reasoning: Reference: Spanish general-election leader debates on combined channels. Nov 2019 five-way drew 8.6M on 12 channels; July 2023 cara a cara 5.9M on two channels; RTVE 2023 three-way ~4M. Linear TV viewing has fallen (170 min/day now vs ~220-240 in 2019), so 8.6M scales to roughly 6-6.5M. Pulls down: this is the second leader debate, a week after the Sanchez-Feijoo cara a cara, plus an eight-party RTVE debate on the 23rd. Pulls up: an intense campaign and possibly broad carriage. RTVE carriage of the 26th is confirmed and the Academia feed is open to all broadcasters, but which private channels join is unconfirmed: Antena 3/laSexta carried the 19th; Mediaset is unknown. No market found (Polymarket/Manifold none; Spain blocked Polymarket/Kalshi in 2026). Median ~5.8M.

calls.reasoning: Anchor is the 2023 regime: 5.9M for the July 2023 cara a cara on two channels, ~4.0M for the RTVE three-way without Feijóo. The 2015-19 figures of 8.6-10.5M reflect much higher linear viewing. The 26 Nov Academia four-way with all four main leaders is confirmed in the press; RTVE carriage is listed, private carriage is unconfirmed. Atresmedia's own 23 Nov four-way and laSexta's Mesa Abierta panel that night suggest private carriage may be thinner than for the 19 Nov cara a cara. November viewing, an intense campaign and the final-debate effect pull up; a second debate within a week and linear decline pull down. Median ~5.4M.
calls.reconciliation: The runs largely agree (medians 5.5-5.8). Factual: the debate date and line-up are agreed across dossiers (Academia four-way, 26 Nov); carriage beyond RTVE cannot be settled without web access, so it carries its full uncertainty. Pointers to thinner private carriage (Atresmedia's own 23 Nov four-way, a laSexta Mesa Abierta panel listed for 26 Nov) put the median slightly below the runs, at 5.4. Judgment calls: the size of the linear-TV decline (anchored on 2023, since 2023 viewing was already near 2026 levels) and fatigue (historically small). Reference class and dispersion are carried forward from the runs with a slightly wider low tail.
